questions.q: What is the IQR rule for flagging outliers?
options: Any value with an absolute z-score above 3
Any value above the mean
Any value more than 1.5 times the IQR below Q1 or above Q3
Any value outside the range 0 to 1000
questions.explain: The IQR rule sets fences at Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR. Box plots use the same rule for whiskers and dots.

questions.q: In the illustrative data, the IQR rule flagged 19 total_spend values but a z-score cutoff of 3 flagged only 2. Why?
options: The two extreme values inflate the mean and standard deviation, which masks the milder outliers
Z-scores are always more sensitive than the IQR rule
Z-scores ignore the largest values
The IQR rule counts missing values
questions.explain: Extreme values pull the mean and inflate the standard deviation, so other high values have smaller z-scores. Quantile-based rules are more robust for skewed data.

questions.q: Two rows had spend per order of 2,450 and 1,480 versus a median of about 37. What is the most sensible next step?
options: Immediately delete every flagged row
Replace them with the mean
Ignore them because outliers do not matter
Investigate why: check for a keying error or bulk purchase, ask the data owner, then decide and document
questions.explain: A flag is a question, not a verdict. Use related columns and domain knowledge to judge, then choose keep, fix, cap, flag, or remove, and record why.

questions.q: Which action limits an outlier's influence without deleting the row?
options: Dropping the entire column
Capping (winsorizing) values at a boundary, such as the 99th percentile
Sorting the DataFrame
Converting the column to strings
questions.explain: Clipping values to a boundary (for example spend.clip(upper=spend.quantile(.99))) keeps the row but caps its leverage on means and correlations.

questions.q: After excluding the two extreme rows, mean spend by channel was about app 158, store 155, web 152. What does this illustrate?
options: The 'app customers spend more' finding was created by two outlying rows, so conclusions should be tested with and without outliers
Channels never differ in spend
Removing rows always improves an analysis
Means are always more reliable than medians
questions.explain: The channel gap appeared only because two huge values landed in the app and web groups. Checking sensitivity to outliers, and documenting the treatment, protects you from findings that are really two rows.
